title: ₹1 Lakh Coaching Fee: Institute Owner Ke Paas Kitna Bachta Hai?
description: Reasoning: our school-fee reel is already covered, and this is the adjacent, higher-stakes question. Almost every Indian family has paid for coaching, so it has high relatability and shareability. Public numbers exist in listed edtech and coaching filings and in industry reports.
text:
# HISAAB FACT SHEET: Coaching Institute Unit Economics (India)

Notes for the scriptwriter:
- There is no audited per-centre P&L for a small local institute anywhere in what I found. Small-centre figures come from blogs and guides, so treat them as estimates and say "estimates vary" on screen.
- The large-chain figures (Allen, PW, Motion) come from filings or reputable news and are solid.
- I found no verified revenue-share percentage for Indian star teachers. Indian star-teacher pay is public only as annual packages.
- Lines marked "(derived)" are simple arithmetic on sourced numbers. Everything else is quoted from a source.

## 1. The hook maths: ₹1 crore from 100 students at ₹1 lakh

- Fee × students: 100 × ₹1 lakh = ₹1 crore (derived from the hook).
- GST is charged on top of the fee. Coaching fees are taxable at 18%, unlike recognised-school fees, which are exempt. [https://www.erpgroup.in/blog/coaching-institute-management-software-india]
- PW Vidyapeeth's price shows the pattern: a Class 11 JEE/NEET fee of ₹49,000 + 18% GST (older figure). [https://brainly.in/question/57806355]
- Script note: check whether the "₹1 lakh" is pre-GST or post-GST.
- One small-institute cost model from a start-up guide: faculty 35%, rent 15%, marketing 10%, operations 5%, giving a net margin of 35%. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
  - Applied to ₹1 crore (derived): faculty ₹35 lakh, rent ₹15 lakh, marketing ₹10 lakh, operations ₹5 lakh, owner keeps ₹35 lakh.
  - This is a "well-managed" blog scenario, not an audited figure.
- Margin claims for small and mid-size centres vary widely by source:
  - Typical margins of 20% to 40% after stabilisation; break-even in 12 to 24 months. [https://www.bajajfinserv.in/coaching-institute-business]
  - Independent tutors 60% to 80%; mid-sized institutes with rented classrooms and faculty salaries 35% to 55%. [https://www.feealert.in/tools/tuition-fee-calculator]
  - Gross margins in coaching typically run 40–65%. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
- Script note: these small-centre margins usually don't pay the owner's own salary. If the owner teaches, that is unpaid labour hidden in the "profit". This is my observation, not from a source.

## 2. Cost to start a small local centre (estimates)

- A basic setup can cost ₹2.5 lakh to ₹5 lakh. [https://www.registerkaro.in/post/how-to-start-a-coaching-institute-india]
- Working capital for 3 months of rent and staff salary before fee income: ₹1.5–₹3 lakh. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
- Fixed costs and break-even: For a Tier-2 institute with monthly fixed costs of ₹1.5–₹2.5 lakh and a fee of ₹5,000–₹8,000/month per student, break-even is about 30–50 students. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
- Typical monthly fees by niche and location: ₹2,000–₹12,000/month. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
- Example revenue: 200 students paying ₹8,000/month = ₹16 lakh monthly revenue. [https://unstopgrowth.com/blog/how-to-start-coaching-institute-india]
- Franchise route (CA coaching, one franchise-broker site):
  - Royalty/brand fee of 10–20% of monthly revenue.
  - Break-even in most cases within 18–36 months, with annual margins of 25–35% from Year 2.
  - [https://www.bivha.in/blog/ca-coaching-franchise-in-india]
- Rules: Coaching operates under state-level education norms, municipal regulations and registration frameworks. [https://www.bajajfinserv.in/coaching-institute-business]
- Under the CCPA 2024 guidelines, a coaching centre is one that coaches more than 50 students. [https://www.medianama.com/2024/11/223-ccpa-new-guidelines-curb-misleading-ads-coaching-sect/]

## 3. Batch size and fee per student (large chains)

- Allen Kota batch size is disputed:
  - One listing shows a batch size of 40-60. [https://collegedunia.com/institute/3426-allen-kota]
  - Another puts it at "Large (100-120)". [https://studyreach.in/allen-kota-result-2026-jee-toppers-list/]
  - An old, unverified Quora answer says 120–200 students per batch, with a "star batch" of around 20 in Class 11 and 30 in Class 12. [https://www.quora.com/How-many-students-are-there-in-one-batch-at-ALLEN-and-Resonance-in-Kota]
  - Script note: don't state one batch size as fact. Say "roughly 100–200 in regular batches; top batch 20–30 (unverified)".
- Allen Kota fees vary by source:
  - Class XI JEE: ₹83,000 - ₹1,72,000 per year. [https://collegedunia.com/institute/3426-allen-kota/courses-fees]
  - Roughly ₹1.5 to 2.5 lakh per year for classroom programs. [https://gauravtiwari.org/best-neet-coaching-centers-in-kota/]
  - Hostel and mess are separate, roughly ₹1.2 to 1.8 lakh per year. [https://gauravtiwari.org/best-neet-coaching-centers-in-kota/]
- PW offline pricing: Vidyapeeth is about ₹77k–₹1.3L (2025 guide). [https://www.notesly.in/article/physics-wallah-iit-jee-coaching-comprehensive-guide-to-affordable-online-batches-vidyapeeth-centre-fees-2025-edition]
- PW revenue actually earned per student is far below the sticker fee:
  - Vidyapeeth in H1 FY27: ₹681.8 crore revenue from 2.53 lakh students, with ARPU (revenue per user) of ₹26,972. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/physicswallah-slows-offline-centre-openings-ppt-cmw3d3sts004o2mphsq418dmz]
  - Earlier: online ARPU ₹4,312 and offline ARPU ₹12,633. [https://www.markhub24.com/post/physics-wallah-s-hybrid-online-and-offline-education-model]
  - Script note: the sources don't explain the gap between sticker fee and ARPU. It could be scholarships, part-period revenue or other factors, so check before claiming a reason.

## 4. Faculty pay (the biggest cost)

- At the Motion chain (FY25), employee benefit expense was ₹49 crore, about 48% of total expenses. [https://thebusinessrule.com/motion-coaching-stalls-at-%E2%82%B9108-cr-trouble-or-smart-survival-strategy/]
- At PW (FY25):
  - Employee expenses were ₹1,401.2 crore, up 21%. [https://inc42.com/buzz/physicswallah-fy25-loss-down-78-to-inr-243-cr-revenue-nears-inr-3000-cr-mark/]
  - That is 48.5% of FY25 revenue. [https://www.businessoutreach.in/physicswallah-business-model/]
  - Headcount is reported inconsist
